title: Dedicated pool surge: adaptive throttling, safe rollback, and RCA-driven remediation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a high-concurrency customer test on 2026-02-27 we observed sustained dedicated-pool throughput collapse and increased tail latency leading to request throttling and degraded customer SLAs. This ticket drives the incident response playbook refinement: coordinate immediate mitigations, validate a safe rollback and throttling mechanism, complete an RCA, and owner-assigned remediation deliverables. The incident surfaced three correlated signals: degraded autoscale decisions, control-plane rate limiting on pool controller, and an unexpected KV cache eviction pattern under specific sequence-length distributions. Goal: restore stable headroom for affected pools, harden autoscale decisions to avoid oscillation, and create deterministic safe-rollback and throttling primitives for Dedicated.

2026-02-27T10:18Z - Teams paged: infra, serving-runtime, routing. Initial mitigation: increase pool target capacity by +15% and enable emergency burst from shared spare capacity
2026-02-27T10:35Z - Observed continued tail latency; rollback of a control-plane change (cookie-based affinity) attempted, no immediate recovery
2026-02-27T11:05Z - Emergency adaptive throttle rule applied to non-critical tenant classes to preserve headroom
2026-02-27T12:00Z - Stable but suboptimal throughput; mitigation held while on-call prepares post-incident playbook
immediate_actions: Applied adaptive throttling to best-effort tenants (rule THR-2026-02) to reduce concurrency on affected pools
Allocated emergency spare GPUs to pool-prod-42 to prevent SLA breaches while root cause analysis runs
Rolled back recent affinity change in control-plane (PR #4821) as a temporary measure
hypotheses: Autoscaler was oscillating due to noisy short-lived traffic spikes and conservative cool-down settings
Control-plane rate limit for pool controller prevented scale-up API calls under heavy reconciliation load
KV cache policy evicted hot prefixes causing repeated cold-attention recomputation with long sequences, amplifying latency
investigations_planned: Correlation of autoscaler decision logs with request-level traces to identify oscillation triggers
Load-replay on staging with preserved sequence-length distribution to reproduce cache eviction and latency amplification
Audit of controller rate-limiting counters and throttling windows during incident window
runbook_changes: Add an 'emergency throttle' step to Dedicated runbook with explicit tenant-classing and guardrails
Document safe rollback criteria for control-plane affinity and routing changes (pre- and post-rollback smoke tests)
Add a short-circuit path in autoscaler: if control-plane rate limit observed, route scale requests through secondary controller
long_term_actions: Implement hysteresis and adaptive cooldown in autoscaler (owner: Mei Chen, due: 2026-04-15)
Upgrade pool controller concurrency model and add leader-election backpressure avoidance (owner: Jorge Alvarez, due: 2026-04-01)
KV cache policy tuning and instrumentation to expose eviction root causes for long-sequence workloads (owner: Lina Gupta, due: 2026-04-20)
Build canary / chaos tests for control-plane rate limiting and verify safe-rollback behavior in pipeline (owner: SRE Team, due: 2026-05-05)
